evidence: Dimension weights: task/tests/scoring.toml:1-11 is byte-identical to the frozen template scoring.toml (diff empty): gates render=0.0, constraints=0.0; weights functional=0.6, polish=0.2, visual=0.2; floors functional=0.05. tools/score.py also identical to template; score.py:40-48 zeroes reward unless gates pass and functional > floor, and computes sum(w*score)/sum(w). Gates carry no reward mass (gates/*/judge.toml aggregation='all_pass', single binary criterion each). Maximum style-only contribution: visual 0.2 of reward (5 likert criteria, all weight 1.2, equal split, visual/judge.toml:22,37,52,67,82). Polish (0.2) is not style: its 5 binary criteria (polish/judge.toml) grade concrete behaviour named in the public brief - preserving open card/note/focus/scroll across live board updates (w3, instruction.md:5), preserving reply draft/focus/newest view on live message (w3, instruction.md:7), keeping place when loading earlier messages (w2, instruction.md:7), failed send keeps text and is not duplicated (w1.5), drafts surviving sign-out with per-user isolation (w2.5, instruction.md:7). So behaviour-backed mass is 0.8 vs style 0.2; real functionality outweighs structure and style. Per-criterion functional weights (sum 59.5 over 44 binary criteria, computed with tomllib): top weight 2.5 on hro_stale_refused, hro_live_board, hro_candidate_private - exactly the brief's stated 'hard part' (instruction.md:1 'nobody's work gets trampled', :3 'tell me who', :5 live board in 15 s, :9 'must never see our internal notes'); 2.0 on all-or-none multi-move, undo restore/conflict, refused put-back (public in hireops_rules.md:85 and instruction.md:3), earlier-message paging, unread counts, scrolled-up notice, drafts; 0.5 on hro_job_open, hro_add_candidate, hro_reject_hired, hro_undo_full, hro_activity_refusals, hro_candidate_linked. The 0.5 rows are either narrow edge refusals or intake prerequisites: functional/prompt.md:27 (S) creates J1/J2 and candidates A-F, V-Z that every later protocol (M, L, B, N, V...) depends on, so a broken intake already zeroes most of Functional; low direct weight avoids double-counting rather than understating real functionality. Each functional criterion is 0.005-0.025 of total reward; each polish criterion 0.025-0.05, which is higher per row but the polish rows are themselves brief-mandated behaviour, not style. Counterexample attempts: (a) a polished-looking but functionally thin app (intake, single moves, reorder, reject/reopen, places; no push, no conversations): about 25/59.5 functional -> ~0.25, polish ~0 (live/thread rows are 0 when no update arrives, per polish/judge.toml:23,32), visual <=0.2 -> <=~0.45, well below a fully working plain-styled app (0.6 + polish up to 0.2 + low visual) - ranking not inverted by weights. (b) a near-dead pretty app just above the 0.05 floor: <= ~0.03 + 0.2 visual + ~0 polish = ~0.23 max; the template-controlled floor is not a task-added choice and gates already exclude non-rendering/constraint-violating apps. (c) a conforming alternative that loses disproportionately: missing live push costs hro_live_board, both polish live rows, unread/seen rows (~0.2 of reward), but live updates are the brief's central demand (instruction.md:5,7), so the mass is honest. No structure-only or source-reading criterion carries weight; the constraints gate (technology/structure) is weight 0. Notes (not defects): RewardKit likert normalisation (n/5 vs (n-1)/4) is not defined in the task bytes, which only shifts the visual floor; reward discrimination/ranking runs are absent per raw-evidence-index.json scope - that is runtime evidence owned by rows 42/43 and the runtime records, not required to judge the static weight design of this row.
